title: Fit the Matching Bit and Power-Tighten a Loose Drawer Knob
instruction: Inspect the loose drawer-knob screw. Fit the matching bit into the stopped powered screwdriver, tighten the screw with that tool, then release the stopped tool in its stand.
context: General maintenance and repair workers routinely secure loose cabinet hardware with interchangeable driver bits. Here the robot must select a bit by the visible recess, fit it into an empty powered driver, steady the free drawer, and tighten its knob screw. A mismatched bit can strip the head; an unsecured drawer can slide. The three bits share a colour, so their working-end shapes distinguish them.
setup: Single-screw side-approach scene; Standard YAM station table, top z=747.5 mm, x away from the robot and y across the table. One free 1.4 kg wooden drawer starts inner-face-up at (322,360,747.5) mm on two fixed dark-polymer supports at (322,205,747.5) and (322,515,747.5) mm, each 146 x 23 x 76 mm. Its front panel is 340 x 146 x 16 mm; a guided dark-polymer knob about 42 x 42 mm starts 1.5 mm loose. Exactly one exposed zinc-steel cross screw has a 12 mm head, at drawer-local (-32,-60,99) mm. A free 320 g polymer/metal powered screwdriver with 52 mm-wide fixed rubber grip faces and no button with empty 6.45 mm hex holder lies horizontally at nominal (225,-15,812.5) mm and settles near (225,-15,814.5) mm, axis -y, on two colliding dark-polymer U supports at (225,-24,747.5) and (225,-106,747.5) mm with a grey 95 x 70 mm visual recessed bed between them and a fixed backstop at (225,63,747.5) mm. The U supports, not the non-colliding visual bed, carry the tool. Three free steel-coloured 14 g, approximately 98 mm overall bits with 90 mm long, 6.35 mm hex shanks and cross, hex or slotted working ends start at (45,-130,817.5), (45,-40,817.5) and (45,50,817.5) mm in separate fixed dark-polymer racks centred at x=85 mm. Three matching 32 x 32 mm dark-polymer profile plaques are centred at x=175 mm on those same three y lanes. See README for detailed geometry, orientations and reset.
scoring: 0 if the correct bit is not stably installed. 0.2 after the cross bit remains in the stopped chuck for 20 control steps with both gripper TCPs more than 60 mm from the bit grip (holding the tool housing is allowed; no return-to-ready is required) and its tip more than 20 mm from the screw. 0.8 after that assembly: while the push-start motor is on, the mounted cross bit must be inside the screw recess (within 1 mm radial, -2.5 to +2.3 mm axial from head centre, within 8 degrees of axis and 15 degrees of cross orientation relative to the rotating head), and corresponding positive spindle rotation, screw rotation, axial feed and knob closure must produce at least 1.3 mm credited feed. Net screw feed must remain at least 1.3 mm and knob gap at most 0.2 mm; after tool withdrawal and both hands clearing the knob, it must resist a 5 N opening load with no more than 0.25 mm deflection for 20 steps. 1.0 adds the motor stopped and the tool released on its two physical U supports, within 25 mm of its initial position and 8 degrees of its complete initial orientation, with both grippers at least 80% open and more than 60 mm from the tool grip. Hold for 1 second: tool translation at most 2 mm, rotation at most 1 degree and spindle change at most 0.02 rad. Credit is capped by net feed and is lost if the bit is no longer mounted; hand turning, free spinning, motor taps and back-out cannot substitute for powered feed.
fidelity: The scene uses procedural rigid bodies and a physical removable hex bit, a push-start spindle without a manual button, and one screw bearing coupled to an axial carriage and guided knob at ideal M4 pitch (0.7 mm/rev). The 12 mm head is enlarged for camera legibility. Resolved helical thread flanks, calibrated clamp preload, material wear/compliance and real-world success are not modeled. The 5 N simulated load is a task check, not product calibration.
scores: Fixed-layout, from-reset scripted YAM demo: 1.0 in 4,291 control steps. Dream-1 beta: 0.0 in one 6,000-step official trial, with zero errored trials.
reset_notes: Put the free drawer inner-face-up on both supports; set the knob gap to 1.5 mm, the one screw bearing angle and axial-feed carriage to zero. Return all three bits to their named racks in their horizontal initial poses, leave the chuck empty and stopped, place the driver in its stand, and return both YAM arms to ready. Check the replacement setup and three camera images before a scored trial.
